model: E5CC / E5EC / E5AC / E5DC digital temperature controllers (E5_C series)
applies_to: Omron E5CC, E5EC, E5AC, E5DC and E5CC-U controllers with RS-485, per the E5_C Communications Manual H175; registers present depend on model and options.
summary: Omron's E5_C temperature controllers speak CompoWay/F or Modbus RTU on their RS-485 option. The variable area can be read in 4-byte mode (two registers per value) or 2-byte mode (one register per value, addresses from 0x2000); this map uses 2-byte mode for PV, set points, MV, heater current, alarms and status, plus the operation-command register for RUN/STOP, auto/manual and auto-tune.

addressing.note: Addresses are printed in hex and sent as-is: the manual's 2-byte example reads PV with 01 03 20 00 00 01. 4-byte mode addresses (0000, 0002, ...) hold the same data as two registers each; only 2-byte mode addresses are listed here.

source.title: E5@C Digital Temperature Controllers Communications Manual
source.pages: Comm parameters p. 1-6; Modbus procedure pp. 4-7 to 4-14 (modes, examples, operation commands); variable area pp. 5-2 to 5-16; status bits pp. 3-23 to 3-25 (PDF pp. 75-77, 96)

notes: Values are sent without the decimal point (105.0 is sent as 1050). PV, set points and alarm values use the decimal places reported by 2410; MV (x0.1 %) and heater current (x0.1 A) have fixed scaling per the setting ranges.
In 2-byte mode 2001 and 2406 return the low 16 bits of the 32-bit status and 2407 the high 16 bits; bit meanings come from the status table on pp. 3-23 to 3-25.
Before any write, send operation command 'communications writing ON' (0x0001 to address FFFF). FC06 single writes work only in 2-byte mode; FC16 works in both.

The manual states a default unit number of 1 and a default send data wait of 20 ms; default baud rate and parity are only shown as highlighted cells, so they are not listed. With Modbus the data length is fixed at 8 bits, with 1 stop bit for even/odd parity or 2 for none.
Left out: the rest of the adjustment, initial-setting and advanced levels (PID, scaling, input type and so on), alarm 3/4 values, valve opening, and program/SP ramp parameters.

integration.summary: Read 0x2000-0x2005 with FC03 for PV, status, internal SP, heater current and MV; read 0x2410 once for the decimal point. To change the set point, first write 0x0001 to 0xFFFF (communications writing ON), then write 0x2103.
integration.enable: Set Protocol Setting (psel) to Modbus in the communications setting level, set unit number and baud, then cycle power. Writes need 'communications writing ON' via the operation command.
quirks: Values carry no decimal point; check 2410.
Use 2-byte mode addresses (0x2000+) for 16-bit tools; 4-byte mode needs even addresses and even counts.
Reading in setup area 1 freezes or clears some status bits.
setup: Protocol (psel), unit no. (u-no, default 1), baud (bps), parity (prty) and send data wait (sdwt, default 20 ms) are set on the front panel in the communications setting level; reset the controller to apply changes.
Up to 106 registers per read in 2-byte mode.
gotchas: In backup mode every communications write of an operation/adjustment parameter is also saved to non-volatile memory; RAM write mode (0x0401) skips that until backup mode or 'save RAM data'.
